question: According to the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, which of the following institutions is responsible for regular and fair elections to the Municipalities?
solution:
The correct answer is __**State Election Commission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, mandates the establishment of the **State Election Commission** in each state to oversee elections at the municipal level.
 
• The State Election Commission is responsible for conducting **regular, free, and fair elections** to the urban local bodies (Municipalities) and rural local bodies (Panchayats).
 
• Under Article 243K and 243ZA of the Indian Constitution, the powers of superintendence, direction, and control of the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of all elections to Panchayati Raj Institutions and Municipalities are vested in the State Election Commission.
 
• The State Election Commission is an independent body, and its composition, tenure, and functions are determined by the respective state governments as per the guidelines of the Constitution.
 
• The Election Commission of India is responsible for conducting elections to the Parliament and State Legislatures, but the **State Election Commission handles local body elections**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **74th Constitutional Amendment Act:**

 
 
• It was enacted in 1992 to provide constitutional status to urban local bodies (Municipalities).
 
• The Act introduced three types of municipalities: Nagar Panchayat, Municipal Council, and Municipal Corporation.
 
• It aimed to strengthen decentralized governance in urban areas.
 
 
 
• **State Election Commissions:**
 
 
• Each state has its own State Election Commission, headed by a State Election Commissioner.
 
• The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor of the state.
 
• The Commission ensures independent and impartial elections to local bodies.
 
 
 
• **Election Commission of India vs. State Election Commission:**
 
 
• The Election Commission of India (ECI) conducts elections to the Parliament, State Legislative Assemblies, and the offices of the President and Vice President.
 
• The State Election Commission conducts elections to Panchayats and Municipalities.
 
• Both bodies operate independently of each other.
 
 
 
• **Articles 243K and 243ZA:**
 
 
• These articles provide for the establishment and functioning of the State Election Commissions.
 
• They empower the State Election Commissions to oversee the preparation of electoral rolls and conduct of elections to Panchayats and Municipalities.
